It is also supported by EK 1.1.B.3, 1.1.B.4, and 1.4.A.5.

The entry accurately represents the limit notation and conditions for the location of a hole in a rational function as specified in EK 1.10.A.2, which states: 'If input values sufficiently close to c correspond to output values arbitrarily close to L, then the hole is located at the point with coordinates (c, L). The corresponding mathematical notation is lim r(x) = L. It should be noted that lim_{x->c-} r(x) = lim_{x->c+} r(x) = lim_{x->c} r(x) = L.'

The implication is reversed: a finite limit alone does not establish a hole; a function may be defined at c. CED 1.10.A.2 begins, “If the graph of a rational function r has a hole at x = c,” and then uses nearby output values to locate it. Locating holes is required by 1.10.A, and 1.11.A.1 also identifies holes as information revealed by factored forms. The entry omits the prerequisite that a hole has been established, with no caution noting it.
